caution: Paraphrases of source-linked publications, not expert-certified identifiers or station occurrences. Dated global IUCN categories are not national DENR status.

items.label: Stream habitat
items.statement: Reported to inhabit clear, rocky, well-oxygenated forest streams and to be fully aquatic.
items.limitation: A published habitat association does not establish presence in an unsurveyed stream.
items.source: Miñarro et al. 2025, PeerJ e18694

items.label: Nocturnal and aquatic activity
items.statement: The 2025 study describes B. busuangensis as a fully aquatic, nocturnal species.
items.limitation: Activity summaries do not rule out daytime sightings.
items.source: Miñarro et al. 2025, PeerJ e18694

items.label: Field study adult body size
items.statement: In the 2022–2023 Busuanga study, researchers grouped adults with snout–vent lengths of approximately 50–90 mm.
items.limitation: These are study-specific age-class bounds, not universal identification thresholds.
items.source: Miñarro et al. 2025, PeerJ e18694

items.label: Measured growth rates
items.statement: The study estimated mean monthly growth of about 1.56 mm for subadults and 0.60 mm for adults in sampled populations.
items.limitation: Growth rates are model-based local study estimates, not guaranteed rates elsewhere.
items.source: Miñarro et al. 2025, PeerJ e18694

items.label: Recapture and return behavior
items.statement: A capture–mark–recapture and displacement study found evidence of site fidelity and return to original capture sites after movements of 10–50 m.
items.limitation: This is the outcome of an experimental study, not a prescribed field-survey action.
items.source: Miñarro et al. 2025, PeerJ e18694

items.label: Documented Philippine island records
items.statement: Amphibian Species of the World lists Busuanga, Culion, Balabac and Palawan islands for this species.
items.limitation: The distribution listing is not confirmation at any individual habitat site.
items.source: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Barbourula busuangensis account

items.label: Taxonomic authority and locality
items.statement: The species authority is Brown and Alcala (1970). The type locality is South Gigante Island, Philippines.
items.limitation: Type-locality provenance does not certify every photographed frog.
items.source: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis insulatus account

items.label: Published insular distribution
items.statement: The specialist taxonomic account places the species on South Gigante Island.
items.limitation: No provincial or island-wide GPS occurrence is inferred from the account.
items.source: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis insulatus account

items.label: Limestone association
items.statement: Amphibian Species of the World reports primary and secondary forest on limestone outcrops on South Gigante Island.
items.limitation: Karst habitat resemblance is not enough for species identification.
items.source: AMNH, Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis insulatus account

items.label: Forested caves and karst
items.statement: A historical IUCN threatened amphibians account describes limestone karst forest and caves in forested lowlands.
items.limitation: The cited account uses the historical combination Platymantis insulata.
items.source: IUCN Threatened Amphibians of the World species profile (historical account)

items.label: Direct development
items.statement: The historical species assessment reports development without a free-swimming tadpole stage.
items.limitation: Reproductive mode is a literature report and was not observed in the present field site.
items.source: IUCN Threatened Amphibians of the World species profile (historical account)

items.label: Habitat pressures in historical reference
items.statement: The older assessment identifies limestone extraction, guano collection and forest encroachment among documented habitat pressures.
items.limitation: This is a historical assessment, not a verified 2026 threat or Philippine DENR status.
items.source: IUCN Threatened Amphibians of the World species profile (historical account)

items.label: Scale arrangement
items.statement: The IUCN SSC Pangolin Specialist Group reports that this species has more dorsal scale rows than other Asian pangolins and smaller scales than Sunda pangolin.
items.limitation: This is not a field-approved photographic key and must be checked in a clear view.
items.source: IUCN SSC Pangolin Specialist Group, Philippine Pangolin species account

items.label: Relative body proportions
items.statement: The specialist account describes a shorter head-and-body to tail-length ratio relative to Sunda pangolin.
items.limitation: Angle, posture and incomplete photographs restrict the use of proportional comparison.
items.source: IUCN SSC Pangolin Specialist Group, Philippine Pangolin species account

items.label: Forest and coastal habitat diversity
items.statement: A 2020 research review reports primary and secondary lowland forest, forest–grassland mosaic and some coastal habitats, including beach forest and mangrove.
items.limitation: Habitat tolerance is not a distribution prediction for an individual survey station.
items.source: Schoppe et al. 2020, Pangolins: Science, Society and Conservation, chapter 7

items.label: Activity and foraging
items.statement: The 2020 research review describes a mostly nocturnal, solitary, partly tree-dwelling species that searches for ants and termites.
items.limitation: These are published tendencies, not a guaranteed detection period or site occupancy.
items.source: Schoppe et al. 2020, Pangolins: Science, Society and Conservation, chapter 7

items.label: Palawan faunal region
items.statement: The 2020 review restricts the published native distribution to the Palawan faunal region.
items.limitation: Published broad distribution is not a confirmed occurrence at a named municipality.
items.source: Schoppe et al. 2020, Pangolins: Science, Society and Conservation, chapter 7

items.label: Dated IUCN global status
items.statement: The IUCN global assessment dated 12 April 2018 records Critically Endangered (criteria A3d+4d), published in 2019.
items.limitation: The dated global category does not supply a separately verified Philippine DENR listing.
items.source: IUCN SSC Pangolin Specialist Group 2019, Red List assessment

items.label: Adult horns and coat
items.statement: The Zoological Society of London describes short, backward-pointing horns on both sexes and a dark brown to greyish coat with lighter markings in some animals.
items.limitation: Horns and coloring alone do not certify an identification from a poor image.
items.source: Zoological Society of London, Tamaraw species reference

items.label: Calf coat
items.statement: A specialist zoo conservation reference reports a reddish-brown calf coat that darkens with age.
items.limitation: Age and color observations must be checked against other field characters.
items.source: Zoological Society of London, Tamaraw species reference

items.label: Grassland and forest
items.statement: The IUCN 2016 assessment lists forest, shrubland and grassland habitats for the tamaraw.
items.limitation: Habitat categories do not indicate automatic site suitability.
items.source: Boyles, Schutz and de Leon 2016, IUCN Red List Tamaraw

items.label: Monitored habitat in Iglit–Baco
items.statement: A long-term field monitoring study describes perennial grassland, secondary forest and bamboo patches across monitored sites in Mount Iglit–Baco.
items.limitation: These are habitats in the published study area, not all Mindoro habitats.
items.source: Oryx, Long-term community-based monitoring of tamaraw

items.label: Mindoro endemic
items.statement: Mammal Diversity Database lists the taxon from Mindoro, Philippines.
items.limitation: Endemic distribution does not prove current occupancy at a specific coordinate.
items.source: ASM Mammal Diversity Database, Bubalus mindorensis

items.label: Dated IUCN global status
items.statement: The 27 April 2016 IUCN assessment records Critically Endangered under C1+2a(ii).
items.limitation: This dated global designation is not an independently checked current DENR national category.
items.source: Boyles, Schutz and de Leon 2016, IUCN Red List Tamaraw
